answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The sparrow multiplier is published, charged in cipher, and bridge lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2720 identities would post 1948 proofs and burn roughly 85 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
